scenario: I volunteer at a winter emergency shelter that becomes overcrowded whenever temperatures drop, and because beds are limited, the shelter prioritizes people with serious medical or physical vulnerabilities. On one especially busy night, I was helping sort intake forms while staff tried to place the last available beds. The temperature outside is dangerously low, so anyone who is unable to be taken in will die from hypothermia outside. A man approached my coworker and pointed out several severe medical conditions he had listed, which would move him to the top of the priority list. Later, I overheard him telling a friend that he had lied about those conditions to nab a spot inside. There are still a handful of highly-vulnerable people waiting to have their intake forms processed. If I secretly move the man's intake form to the bottom of the priority list, his bed will go to someone highly-vulnerable. If I do not do this, a highly-vulnerable person will be turned away and left to die from hypothermia.
choice: I decide to secretly move the man's intake form to the bottom of the priority list

outcomes: A highly-vulnerable person is admitted to the shelter
The man who lied is turned away from the shelter
A highly-vulnerable person survives the freezing night
